chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad from Ismail from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him) said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Regarding the one upon whom is the walking during the Hajj, when he pelts the Jamarat, he visits the House riding, and there is nothing upon him.

key_terms.الْمَشْيُ: Walking (specifically as a vow or obligation)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for someone who vowed to walk during Hajj but rides the Kaaba?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Rida (AS), quoting his father Imam al-Sadiq (AS), clarifies that riding during the Tawaf after stoning the Jamarat does not invalidate a vow to perform Hajj on foot, as the obligation of walking is fulfilled by the journey itself rather than the specific mode of transport for every ritual. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the flexibility of vows (nadhr) when ease is available, distinguishing between the core act of pilgrimage and the manner of its execution. It underscores the principle that unless the vow explicitly restricts the mode of transport for all rituals, riding for convenience does not incur a penalty.
